transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Rachel (CTO), Marcus (Head of Platform), Sophie (Security Lead), Evan (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough): OrbitCare wants to expand capacity and go multi-region, evaluating Dedicated capacity for lower latency in EU/APAC. Security has questions about KMS, audit logs and data residency. Procurement needs pricing tiers to close before end of month.

[00:00:05] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call and then we'll jump into your renewal intentions.
[00:00:12] Rachel (CTO): Hey, hi. Rachel here. We have Marcus, Sophie and Evan with me. Thanks for the agenda.
[00:00:18] Liam (SE): Hi all, Liam from Redwood. I'll run through the performance / benchmark asks later.
[00:00:23] Marcus: Morning, afternoon, depends where you are. Yes, thanks.

[00:01:10] Maya: Okay so per the notes you sign up for the base committed tier last year. You're seeing consistent growth in inference volume and you're asking about bumping up reserved capacity and adding EU + APAC regions, correct? Can you frame timing?
[00:01:28] Rachel: Yes. We're hitting the throttling points on our EU traffic, especially for chat and embeddings. We want EU live by end of October and APAC in Q1 but procurement wants committed pricing and a clear plan.
[00:01:45] Evan (Procurement): Yep fiscal quarter close pressure. We need a pricing worksheet with committed tiers and uplift for regional add-ons.

[00:02:30] Liam: Quick technical note — there's two primary paths: hosted with regional model routing vs Redwood Dedicated pools in region. Hosted is faster to stand up but Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower p50/p95 latency. We can also do hybrid: hosted for non-sensitive traffic, Dedicated for peak workloads.
[00:02:50] Marcus: Latency matters for our triage flows. P95 under 220ms in EU is the target. Will Dedicated guarantee that?
[00:03:02] Liam: We target latency SLOs on Dedicated with SLA-backed uptime and tailed latency targets; we can share recent perf curves. It also depends on model family and sequence length. We'll run the benchmark with your sample to show expected p95.

[00:04:25] Sophie: From security: we need KMS integration — customer-managed keys preferred — and we need to validate audit logs and retention. Also data residency questions: will user message content stay in-region?
[00:04:38] Maya: Good call. For Private and Dedicated there are options: customer-managed KMS in Private deployment, and for Hosted we offer encryption at rest and bring-your-own-key via KMS integrations for Dedicated/Private.
[00:04:56] Sophie: There were some mentions of Redwood Dedicated in the docs but last time I saw an earlier PDF it referenced partial key escrow, I want to confirm that's not the case.
[00:05:08] Liam: We'll share an updated security pack. Short answer: we don't hold private key material for customer KMS; keys can stay in customer's KMS/HSM, and audit logs are exportable. We'll include the SOC2 and detailed KMS integration note in the package.

[00:06:45] Marcus: On routing — if we go multi-region, what's the fallback behavior when a regional pool is saturated? We can't afford 5–10s tail calls.
[00:06:55] Liam: Smart routing can fallback to a compatible model variant in a different region or queue to a burst pool. We can configure policies: strict local-only (no fallback) or permissive (fallback to near region). Recommend permissive for early ramp and strict after steady-state.

[00:07:40] Rachel: Is there any cost delta on token pricing between hosted model in-region vs dedicated node usage? We need unit economics for procurement.
[00:07:48] Maya: Yes, hosted per-token pricing differs from reserved Dedicated pricing. Dedicated has a commitment with lower per-unit cost for high throughput. We'll put exact numbers in the pricing worksheet but expect Dedicated to significantly reduce per-token cost for your peak patterns.

[00:09:12] Evan: Can we get a worked example. Say we commit to 4x RTX pools for EU, what's uplift and expected monthly cost vs current hosted spend?
[00:09:20] Maya: We'll model that in the worksheet. Also include burst configs and autoscale caps so you can compare committed vs on-demand.

[00:10:05] Liam: About quantization / model variant — for cost reduction we recommend quantized variants for non-critical responses; full float for high-quality generation. That reduces GPU memory and raises throughput. We can test two variants during the benchmark.

[00:11:30] Sophie: On compliance, we're SOC2 plus a few local data residency regs in EU. We need a written guarantee that logs with PII won't be replicated outside region.
[00:11:42] Liam: For Dedicated/Private we can constrain egress to the region. For hosted we have region pinning with contractual terms — we'll include language for data residency and egress controls in the SOW.

[00:12:55] Marcus: Timeline check: if procurement signs PO by Sept 26, what's the earliest EU activation?
[00:13:04] Maya: If PO 9/26, we can prioritize capex and target EU activation in mid-October (2–3 weeks for Dedicated pool provisioning plus validation). We'll coordinate with your infra for network peering and DNS cutovers.

[00:15:00] Rachel: What about private deployment? We've had internal debate about VPC vs hosted. Private seems heavy but gives the KMS control we want.
[00:15:08] Liam: Private (VPC/on-prem) is more work but satisfies strict sovereignty. There's an on-prem packaged option for air-gapped cases. For OrbitCare, a VPC-based private control plane in EU would meet your KMS and residency requirements with moderate ops overhead.

[00:16:20] Evan: Procurement question: do you prefer an amendment to our existing MSA or a fresh SOW?
[00:16:27] Maya: Usually an SOW amendment works for committed capacity changes. We'll draft an amendment template and share it with your legal and procurement.

[00:18:05] Sophie: A security nit: we need to know access controls for support engineers on the private deployment. RBAC and SSO are non-negotiable.
[00:18:14] Liam: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC. For private deployments we can restrict support access and require just-in-time elevated permissions. We'll put exact controls in the doc.

[00:20:40] Marcus: Can we do a short pilot for EU: Dedicated pool with a capped commit for 30 days? We want to simulate traffic and validate p95.
[00:20:48] Maya: Yes — we can do a 30-day pilot with a time-limited commitment or a provisional reserved pool. We'll include pilot terms in the pricing worksheet.

[00:22:05] Liam: Action item for us: run a 72-hour throughput benchmark using your test dataset and a mix of chat/embedding/long-seq prompts. We will provide raw logs and p50/p95 curves.

[00:24:10] Rachel: Great. Also, one more feature ask: can the rollout be canaryed for 10% users in EU to monitor quality drift?
[00:24:18] Liam: Yes, Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallbacks if quality regressions are detected — we can wire your eval prompts into quality checks and alerts.

[00:25:50] Evan: On billing, is there a monthly invoice model for committed capacity? We prefer net-30 but need to confirm.
[00:26:00] Maya: Net-30 is standard for enterprise; we'll note that in the SOW and include invoicing cadence options.

[00:28:12] Sophie: Regarding audit logs retention — can we configure retention windows and export to our SIEM?
[00:28:19] Liam: Yes, logs are exportable (S3, Kafka link) and retention windows configurable in Private and Dedicated, with limited retention for Hosted. We'll document the exact endpoints.

[00:31:30] Rachel: Any blockers from your side for the mid-October target?
[00:31:36] Maya: No blockers. We need timely PO and Marcus' team to provide test dataset and peering info.

[00:33:02] Marcus: We'll get the sample dataset and network contact over by 9/15.

[00:34:20] Maya: Recap: we'll send pricing worksheet and pilot terms by 9/15; Liam runs the benchmark and uploads by 9/19; Sophie will send compliance questions by 9/16; Evan to send procurement template by 9/17. Target signature week of 9/29.

[00:35:00] Sophie: Quick clarification — for KMS do you support customer HSMs?
[00:35:06] Liam: Yes, Cold HSM integrations supported for Private; for Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS providers and HSM-backed keys. We'll detail the options.

[00:36:35] Evan: Who will be our go-to contact for technical escalations during pilot?
[00:36:40] Liam: I'll be primary SE; Maya will be your AE; we'll set up a dedicated Slack channel for the pilot.

[00:38:10] Rachel: Sounds good. Any last open concerns?
[00:38:17] Marcus: Just the p95 guarantees — we'll need the benchmark to verify.
[00:38:24] Liam: Understood. We'll make the benchmark as close to your production mix as possible.

[00:40:00] Maya: Alright thanks everyone — we'll lo g these actions. Appreciate the time.
[00:40:07] Evan: Thanks.
[00:40:10] Sophie: Thanks all.
[00:40:15] Rachel: Bye.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions of product names (e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" heard as "Redwood Dedicate"), filler words, and speaker overlaps.

End of call.
